challenges.title: Caesar's Last Words
challenges.description:
A retired professor left one encrypted sentence on the club whiteboard before disappearing into the Tunisian summer.

```
FAG{p4rf4e_j0hyq_o3_ce0hq}
```

It looks almost like a flag, which is the point: classical ciphers preserve shape. Shift it back.

hints.text: The alphabet has 26 letters. Try 25 wrong answers quickly.
ROT13 is a Caesar shift with a very specific key.

challenges.title: Base Instincts
challenges.description:
Encoding is not encryption, and the portal proves it twice a minute.

After login the API returns a bearer token: three dot-separated segments, no signature anyone verifies. The middle segment is just JSON wearing a different alphabet.

**Goal:** decode the token payload and submit the value it leaks.

Careful: this is `base64url`, not `base64` — no padding, and `-`/`_` replace `+`/`/`.

hints.text: Three segments: header, payload, signature. Only one of them carries data.
Base64url drops the `=` padding and swaps `+`/`/` for `-`/`_`. Add the padding back before decoding.

challenges.title: XOR Toddler
challenges.description:
Every flag starts with `SNT{`. Every ciphertext here was produced by XOR-ing each byte with the same single-byte key.

That means you already know the first four bytes of the plaintext — and therefore the first four bytes of the key.

**Goal:** recover the key, decrypt the message.

hints.text: XOR is its own inverse: ciphertext ⊕ key = plaintext.
'S' is 0x53. XOR it with the first ciphertext byte to get the key.

challenges.title: Nonce Sense
challenges.description:
A backup tool encrypts every file with AES-256-CTR. It generates one random nonce at startup and reuses it for every file in the batch — because "random is slow".

You have two ciphertexts of different lengths, both starting with the same known header.

**Goal:** recover the keystream and decrypt the second file.

hints.text: In CTR mode, C = P ⊕ keystream. Same nonce means same keystream.
C1 ⊕ C2 = P1 ⊕ P2. With a known P1, P2 falls out.

challenges.title: RSA for Toddlers
challenges.description:
A home-made licence server encrypts its licence blobs with RSA and chose `e = 3` because "smaller is faster". Messages are short and unpadded.

You have the public key and one ciphertext. The math does not need a quantum computer.

**Goal:** recover the plaintext without factoring the modulus.

hints.text: When m³ is smaller than n, the modulus never wraps. Take a cube root.
If it does wrap a little, search for m such that m³ mod n is the ciphertext.

challenges.title: Padding Oracle Express
challenges.description:
The session cookie is AES-CBC encrypted, and the server answers with three different error messages depending on why decryption failed. That difference is a decryption oracle.

**Goal:** decrypt an existing cookie byte by byte, then forge one whose plaintext contains `role=admin`. No key needed.

hints.text: Each byte of the previous block controls one byte of the next plaintext after decryption.
Aim for padding 0x01, then 0x02 0x02, and so on. 256 tries per byte at worst.
